clue.text: Flowering closer somehow in garden boundary

indicators.note: in says the shuffled letters go inside the boundary word

parts.note: a fence is what marks off a garden

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of closer are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A gardener notices blooms appearing closer to the fence at the edge of the plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closer' reads as a comparative of close but is just anagram fodder, its letters set inside the boundary after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists use this word for the act or period of blooming, a direct synonym.

clue.text: What the crystal ball presages: money will get crucial

parts.note: a fortune is a large sum of money
a telling point is a decisive, crucial one

explanation.surface: A fairground mystic promises the client cash will be decisive in their future.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazing into a crystal ball is a stock method of predicting someone's future, the clairvoyant's trade.

clue.text: Nothing very old, mind (odd bits excepted) — like the curate's egg?

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: leaving out the odd-numbered letters of mind keeps only its second and fourth

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about a mind being empty and ancient, compared to something only good in parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The curate's egg comes from a Punch cartoon: a timid curate served a bad egg says parts of it are excellent. Here only its shape matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid means egg-shaped, which describes any egg, the curate's included; the question mark flags the definition by example.

clue.text: Sheep being trimmed in smaller numbers

indicators.note: trimming cuts away both ends of the word for smaller numbers

parts.note: in smaller numbers means fewer

explanation.surface: A flock is shorn and seems to shrink in number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being trimmed' takes the first and last letters, F and R, off FEWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep has its own name, so the general word for the animal stands in for it.

clue.text: Study research funding, say, as a means of atonement

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
science money is a plausible description of a research grant, 'say' marking the phrase as loose

explanation.surface: An academic pitches their grant application as a way of making amends.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment made anonymously to ease a guilty mind, such as unpaid tax sent in later, makes amends for a wrong.

clue.text: Note monarch, in time before festival, displaying self-possession

indicators.note: in places the monarch's letter inside the word for the time before a festival

parts.note: an eve is the evening or day before a festival, as with Christmas Eve
R stands for Rex or Regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A record of a king arriving on the eve of a feast, composed and calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monarch' is R here, not the more common ER: N then E(R)VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve is coolness and courage under pressure, which is keeping one's composure.

clue.text: Time and space mostly set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means read upwards, so backwards
mostly drops the last letter of the word for space

parts.note: an area is a space

explanation.surface: Time and space are largely constructed, a physics musing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts AREA to ARE, and 'set up' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a period of history, a span of time.

clue.text: Halts indolence if this is damaged? On the contrary!

definitions.text: Halts indolence if this is damaged? On the contrary!

indicators.text: if this is damaged? On the contrary!
indicators.note: the clue claims damaging the answer gives halts indolence; on the contrary, damaging halts indolence gives the answer, so those words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A joke that an injured heel would stop laziness, when really such an injury enforces rest.
explanation.walkthrough: A reversed anagram: jumbling the answer would give HALTS INDOLENCE, so jumble that phrase instead. The heel injury in fact causes idleness rather than halting it.
explanation.definitionFit: This heel tendon is the classic sports injury that halts activity, the opposite of ending laziness.

clue.text: What the hippies sought: extra love amongst the trees?

indicators.note: amongst places the extra letter inside the word for trees

parts.note: a grove is a small group of trees
love is zero in tennis, the letter O, here an extra one

explanation.surface: Flower children wandering into the woods seeking more free love.
explanation.definitionFit: In 1960s slang a groove was a pleasurable rhythm or state, what hippies wanted to be 'in'.

clue.text: No railway includes line maintained by Scotsman? That's the usual state of affairs

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: includes wraps the railway abbreviation round what follows
maintained by puts the line's letter inside the Scotsman's word, held there

parts.note: Mac, from the Gaelic for son, is a familiar name for a Scotsman

explanation.surface: A Scottish signalman keeps a line going where there is no railway, which is supposedly normal.
explanation.definitionFit: Normalcy, an American-flavoured synonym of normality, means things being as they usually are.

clue.text: Hints Bill embraces lady in odd positions in closed-off area

indicators.note: embraces wraps the word for hints round the picked letters

parts.note: cues are hints or prompts

indicators.note: taking the first and third letters of lady gives its odd positions

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Someone drops hints that a man named Bill is holding a woman in a secluded spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is AC, an account.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead-end street, sealed at one end, is literally an area closed off to through traffic.

clue.text: Winter sportsman very quietly easing away from captain

indicators.note: easing away from means the soft marking slips out of the word for captain

parts.note: a skipper is a captain
PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quietly

explanation.surface: A sportsman slips silently away from the team captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on skis on snowy slopes takes part in a classic winter sport.

clue.text: Old Testament filling American's heart regarding sex

indicators.note: filling puts the Testament abbreviation inside the central letters

parts.note: the central four letters of the word American are E, R, I, C

explanation.surface: Scripture lies at the core of American views on sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' here means the middle four letters of AMERICAN, not just its central pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotic describes what arouses or concerns sexual desire, so it relates to sex.

clue.text: Vegetable, something not to be considered, on reflection? I will tuck in

indicators.note: tuck in places the I inside the reversed letters
on reflection mirrors the phrase, reading it backwards

parts.note: a no-no is something not to be done or considered

explanation.surface: Someone decides after all to eat a vegetable they had ruled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck in' sounds like eating but places I inside ONON.
explanation.definitionFit: This bulb used in cooking is a familiar kitchen vegetable.

clue.text: Certain skill Liberal held in reserve for part of speech

parts.note: definite means certain
art is skill

indicators.note: held in puts the party letter inside the word for reserve

parts.note: ice is reserve or coolness of manner

explanation.surface: A political commentator notes a Liberal kept a certain talent in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar classes the word 'the' as a word type, one of the parts of speech in many schemes.

clue.text: Judge, escaping harm, has to get tougher

indicators.note: escaping means the judge's letter gets out of the word for harm

parts.note: to injure is to harm

explanation.surface: A judge avoiding injury must harden up.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure is to accustom to hardship, making someone hardened against it.

clue.text: Government in control in time in power

indicators.note: in places the government letter inside the word for control

parts.note: a rein is a means of control

explanation.surface: A government in control for its period in office.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's period on the throne is their rule's span, so the time spent ruling.

clue.text: Hare? Scut entire, sir, or somewhat damaged

indicators.note: somewhat damaged means the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A rabbit's tail is asked about: is it whole, or rather the worse for wear?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hare' is not the animal but William Hare, partner of Burke, who in 1820s Edinburgh murdered people to sell bodies for dissection. A scut is a hare's short tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Body-snatchers who dug up corpses for anatomists were so named; Hare is an infamous example.

clue.text: Easily flowing in pipe, not empty

parts.note: a flue is a pipe or duct for smoke

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its inside letters, leaving its two ends

explanation.surface: Water runs freely through a pipe that isn't empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluent speech or prose moves smoothly and without effort, just as a stream does.

clue.text: Explosive pervaded by a current contamination

indicators.note: pervaded by means the explosive has the following letters spread inside it

parts.note: TNT, trinitrotoluene, is an explosive
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An explosive charged with current becomes contaminated.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a trace of something bad, a spoiling or polluting presence.

clue.text: Chap embracing elected parliamentarian

indicators.note: embracing means the word for a man wraps round the word for elected

parts.note: mister is a form of address for a man, a chap
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: A man hugs the newly elected MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A government member holding a department is drawn from those sitting in Parliament.

clue.text: Affliction around night-time, primarily

indicators.note: around puts the word for affliction about the picked letter

parts.note: a sore is an affliction, a painful spot

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of night-time

explanation.surface: A complaint that strikes mainly at night.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a nuisance that comes around bedtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy breathing in sleep is a nightly affliction, mostly for the partner lying awake.

clue.text: Popular group heading off lack of engagement

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of the word for group

parts.note: a faction is a group within a party

explanation.surface: A popular band breaking up leaves fans with nothing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing nothing, neither acting nor taking part, is a failure to engage.

clue.text: Against clubs playing?

parts.note: C abbreviates clubs, the card suit
on means playing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: Someone objecting to clubs being played at cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pros and cons are arguments for and against, so con means opposing.

clue.text: Obscure flash in college yard

parts.note: flash and loud both mean showy or garish

explanation.surface: Something murky glimpsed in a college quad.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloudy water or reasoning is murky and unclear, hard to see through.

clue.text: Life-force a bit reduced

indicators.note: reduced cuts the last letter off the word for a bit

parts.note: a chip is a small bit

explanation.surface: A person's vitality is somewhat diminished.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chinese thought qi, also spelt this way, is the vital energy flowing through the body.

clue.text: Homer's error is someone else's problem

definitions.meaning: a homing pigeon landing in the wrong loft would be disowned by that loft's owner
the idiom disclaims responsibility for a matter

explanation.surface: A poet's blunder is passed off as another person's concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' is not the poet or Simpson but a homing pigeon.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, meaning not my concern, comes from pigeon in the old sense of business or affair.
